title: Keel applies identical deposit limits across different protocols and assets, so rate limits do not encode venue risk
content:
Every deposit rate limit in this chunk is the same shape and the same magnitude: `maxAmount` 25,000,000 and `slope` 10,000,000 per day, for Kamino PYUSD (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.1.5.2.4.1), Drift USDS, Drift USDC, Drift USDT and Drift PYUSD. Only the denominating asset changes.

The limits therefore carry no information about relative risk. Two different lending protocols, and four different stablecoins with materially different issuer, redemption and liquidity profiles, are all throttled at exactly the same velocity.

This is a real and readable design position rather than an oversight: rate limits are being used as a *uniform circuit breaker* — a cap on how fast anything can move, applied everywhere — not as a risk-weighting instrument. Risk differentiation, if it happens, must therefore live elsewhere: in the decision to open an Instance at all, in total allocation sizing, or in the RRC Framework whose coverage these documents still mark as `Pending`.

The consequence for a reader auditing Keel is that you cannot infer Keel's risk view of a venue from its conduit parameters. The parameters tell you the maximum speed of movement; they tell you nothing about whether Keel considers Drift safer than Kamino.
description: Kamino and Drift Instances all carry a 25,000,000 maxAmount and 10,000,000-per-day slope regardless of asset (USDS, USDC, USDT, PYUSD)
